name: Carnosine

lead: Carnosine is a dipeptide of beta-alanine and histidine found in muscle and brain, and it appears in some skincare products and supplements positioned for antioxidant and anti-glycation benefits.
Skin-related data are preliminary, mostly from lab studies and small trials, while its best human evidence is as a source of beta-alanine for muscle buffering.

paras: Carnosine scavenges reactive oxygen species, chelates metal ions and inhibits glycation, the process of sugars cross-linking proteins like collagen. These effects are demonstrated mainly in vitro.
It is generally well tolerated; beta-alanine supplementation can cause tingling. Evidence for visible skin improvement is limited.
